lower_bound.quote:
every infinite family of distinct finite sets has an infinite subfamily $X_{i_1},X_{i_2},\ldots$ for which there is a fixed set $R$ satisfying
\[
X_{i_j}\cap X_{i_k}=R\qquad(j\ne k).
\tag{3}
\]
lower_bound.witness: Counterexample: let $X_n=\{1,2,\ldots,n\}\cup\{-n\}$. These are distinct finite sets. If $n_1<n_2<n_3$, then $X_{n_1}\cap X_{n_2}=\{1,\ldots,n_1\}$ whereas $X_{n_2}\cap X_{n_3}=\{1,\ldots,n_2\}$. Thus no subfamily of even three sets, hence no infinite subfamily, has a fixed pairwise intersection.
lower_bound.load_bearing: This false sunflower assertion is the supplied proof of Lemma 1. Lemma 1 is then used to make the terminal family, its union $P$, and consequently the set of relevant primes finite.

parsed.notes: The characterization and periodicity assembly are complete. The claimed global conclusion has the right form, but the written finiteness proof relies on a false infinite-sunflower lemma; the bounded-rank version needed here is not separately proved.
